title: Seasonal Variability in Nutrient Sources and Phytoplankton Primary Productivity in a Shellfish Culture Area of Miyazu Bay, Sea of Japan
content:
ABSTRACT

Phytoplankton primary production is essential to coastal food webs. However, the roles of different nutrient sources in semienclosed bays characterized by strong seasonal variability in physical conditions and nutrient availability are not well understood. We investigated seasonal variations in phytoplankton biomass and primary productivity over 2 years (June 2021–November 2023) at a shellfish aquaculture site in Miyazu Bay, Japan, where nutrients are supplied via offshore seawater intrusion and river discharge as well as submarine groundwater discharge (SGD). Vertically integrated chlorophyll a (Chl-a) and electron transport rate-based primary production were highest in winter, coinciding with elevated dissolved inorganic nutrient concentrations associated with offshore water inputs. However, Chl-a-specific productivity and photosynthetic activity declined in winter due to reduced solar radiation, indicating that phytoplankton biomass accumulated under nutrient-rich conditions despite light limitation. Photosynthetically active radiation (PAR) within the water column was governed primarily by surface PAR rather than by the light attenuation coefficient, which was low and showed no seasonality. In contrast, Chl-a-specific productivity and photosynthetic activity peaked in summer, when surface nutrient concentrations were low but solar radiation was high. Geochemical tracers (222Rn and 224Ra) revealed continuous inputs of nutrient-rich groundwater near the seabed, suggesting that SGD may supplement nutrient availability during nutrient-depleted summer conditions. Size-fractionated analyses revealed that small phytoplankton (< 20 μm) dominated biomass and production throughout the year. These results also highlight SGD as a relatively persistent nutrient pathway that may supplement nutrient availability under light-rich but nutrient-poor summer conditions.
